citation: Wood engravings in A. T. Andreas, History of Chicago, vol. 2 (Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885): 'Tribune Building' and its ruins, p. 492; 'Palmer House' (the first, of 1870), p. 509; 'Potter Palmer Building' (Field, Leiter & Co.'s store, so indexed), p. 563.
author: Blomgren Bros., engravers, Chicago (signed on the Palmer House plate)
describes_date: 1868-1871, the buildings before the fire, and the Tribune building's walls after it
repository: Internet Archive, item historyofchicago02andr (printed pages 492, 509 and 563). The engravings are committed at data/sources/assets/landmarks_1871_t3688/andreas_v2_p492_tribune_building.jpg, andreas_v2_p492_tribune_ruins.jpg, andreas_v2_p509_palmer_house.jpg and andreas_v2_p563_field_leiter_building.jpg.
locator: p. 492: the Tribune building from across Madison and Dearborn Streets to the north-west, its Madison Street front at left, the cut-off corner with the entrance and 'CHICAGO TRIBUNE' over it, the Dearborn Street front at right; beside it, its burnt-out walls. p. 509: the Palmer House from across State and Quincy Streets to the south-east, the Quincy Street front at left, the State Street front with its entrance pavilion and balcony at right, the mansard in two tiers. p. 563: Field, Leiter & Co.'s store from across State and Washington Streets to the south-west, the State Street front at left, the Washington Street front at right, the corner and end pavilions' tall mansards.
rights_note: Published 1885 in the United States; public domain.
